critique: A pale dotted oval/ripple-like particle pattern is visible in a stable lower-frame zone, but it reads as a single loose cloud of dots rather than small, clean water ripples. There are still no visible falling drops or rain streaks in the upper frame, so the required drop-to-impact causality is absent. The two sampled frames also show nearly the same ring state, making expansion difficult to read.

suggestions.why: The rain particles need enough lifetime to travel from the emitter above the frame down to the waterline and become visible before impact.
Larger rain particles will make the falling drops and motion-blurred streaks legible against the dark background.
Narrowing the rain emitter width keeps the visible falling drops near the ripple source, improving the perceived landing relationship.
Reducing ripple particle velocity keeps each burst as a smaller, more readable impact ripple instead of a broad dotted oval.
Use less dense, more frequent ripple bursts with a period that does not align identically between the two review times, making changing expansion states clearer.
Keep the paired live emission synchronized with the revised ripple generations.
